page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-2 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the c4d family. It is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 15.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 7.5 GB per vCPU. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures that the instance does not suffer from resource contention typical of shared-core environments.

This instance does not include local NVMe SSD storage, meaning all persistent storage must be network-attached. It features zero integrated GPUs and does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses. These specifications represent a tradeoff, focusing resources on memory capacity rather than local IOPS or hardware-accelerated computing.

Qualitatively, the c4d-highmem-2 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that require minimal compute power. It is well-suited for applications such as small-scale databases, caching layers, and lightweight enterprise applications that benefit from a higher memory-to-core ratio without the overhead of additional vCPUs.
